sections.h2: Office address, phone and recording cutoff
sections.html:
You will find the office at 110 West Center Street in Lexington, NC 27292. The mailing address is P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. Call 336-242-2150, or fax 336-238-2318. The building is open weekdays 8am to 5pm and closed on county holidays, but the counter stops taking recordings at 4:30pm sharp. That cutoff has applied since August 1, 2020.

The office handles real estate records, vital records, military service records and the notary oath. Counter visits get same-day recording and same-day return of vital records, and a public computer lab and self-serve kiosks are there for legal searches.

The county counts about 180,182 residents and 79,412 housing units. Three in four occupied homes are owner-occupied (74.4 percent), at a median value of $219,100. About 92.2 percent of residents were in the same home a year earlier, so few houses change hands in a typical year.

Real estate searches run through the county's deeds search site, with records indexed from 1984 to the present. For anything older, contact staff directly.

  • To find a paid-off mortgage, search the document type Release.
  • Judgments are looked up through the Clerk of Courts office instead.
  • Attorneys are encouraged to use an e-record system or submit by mail.
  • Color-coded plats do not upload properly and will not be recorded.

The office also posts answers to common questions: whether an instrument must be notarized, whether you can prepare your own deed, and whether you must be present to record.

The counter turns away any real property deed that lacks a certificate from the Tax Administrator showing no overdue tax on the parcel. The rule has applied since March 1, 2019 and rests on G.S. 161-31.

A closing run by an attorney gets around the certificate. The deed instead carries a printed line stating that a North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any overdue tax will be paid to the collector from the sale money. Without an attorney, ask the Tax Department for a certificate through its online form. It can take up to two business days. If you are selling on your own, file the request well before closing, since an unpaid earlier bill will stop the deed at the window.

Most fees are the uniform amounts set in state law (G.S. 161-10). Two more are printed on the county's own page.

Recording charges at the Davidson County office
Document or serviceAmount
Ordinary instrument$26.00 covers 15 pages; each page past that is $4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 covers 35 pages; each page past that is $4.00
Satisfaction or cancellation of a loanFree
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for the first page, $2.00 for each next page
Assumed business name filing$26.00
Card payments3% convenience fee or $1 minimum

Excise tax on the deed is billed apart from these fees: one dollar per $500 of price, counting any part of $500. Sellers pay it up front at the counter.

sections.h2: Why recording protects buyer and seller
sections.html:
G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from a deed, an option or a long lease until it is registered in the county, and whoever registers first ranks first.

So whether you sell in Lexington, Thomasville, Denton or a rural township, treat recording as the last step of the sale, not an afterthought. Ask your closing attorney for the recorded book and page, plus proof that the earlier deed of trust was released.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax bill when a house sells
sections.html:
Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 is billed for the year, and selling later in the year does not clear that owner of the bill. Closings usually split the bill by date, so read the settlement statement to see whether the buyer's portion was credited.

To be safe, ask that the collector be paid straight from closing funds. The collector answers at 336-242-2180 and also issues the certificates the Register of Deeds asks for. A certificate and a recorded deed depend on each other, so clearing the tax account first usually avoids a delay at the recording counter.

Besides deeds, the office takes military discharges and assumed business name filings by mail at P.O. Box 464. Marriage license applications are online, and the applicant then calls to schedule an appointment. A marriage license is valid for 60 days only.

Funeral homes with escrow accounts send certificate requests by fax, and orders are mailed within 48 hours. Others bring the request with payment and proof of their funeral home status, or mail it with a stamped return envelope. If you inherited a house and are selling it, you will likely need death certificates for the estate file. Order several at once.

sections.h2: What to bring on recording day
sections.html:
Arrive before 4:30pm with the signed, notarized deed, the tax certificate or the attorney's printed line on the deed, and payment for the excise tax and the filing fee. A deed of trust or other instrument that runs past the page allowance picks up $4.00 for each added page, so count pages before you go. Card payments add a 3% convenience fee or $1 minimum, which makes a check the cheaper choice for a large amount.

The counter gives same-day recording, so you should leave with confirmation. If an attorney is handling the sale, they typically file for you, and you only need the book and page afterward. Save that reference with your closing papers, because a later buyer's title search will start from it. Questions about timing or a rejected document can go to the office at 336-242-2150 before you make the trip.

sections.h2: Checklist before the deed goes in
sections.html:
A sensible order for a seller handling the details:

  • Look up the parcel's tax bill for any delinquency.
  • Decide whether an attorney will close the sale or you will request a tax certificate yourself.
  • Check that the deed names its preparer and gives a return address.
  • Arrange payment of the excise tax and filing fee for the same day.
  • Obtain the loan payoff figure and a recorded release of the deed of trust.

A loan in default goes to a power-of-sale hearing before the clerk of superior court, and an upset bid can be filed for ten days after the sale is reported. Request the lender's payoff statement in writing right away. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but the certificate, excise tax and filing fee still apply.

faqs.q: What time does the Davidson County Register of Deeds stop recording?
faqs.a: 4:30pm sharp, though the office stays open until 5pm Monday through Friday. The cutoff has applied since August 1, 2020.

faqs.q: Why was my Davidson County deed refused for taxes?
faqs.a: Since March 1, 2019, a real property deed is accepted only with a Tax Administrator certificate showing no delinquent taxes, or under a closing attorney who agrees to pay any delinquent taxes from the proceeds. The certificate can take up to two business days.

faqs.q: How far back do the online Davidson County land records go?
faqs.a: Records are indexed from 1984 to the present. For earlier records, call the office at 336-242-2150.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Davidson County deed?
faqs.a: The seller does, at the counter, before filing. The rate is one dollar for each $500 of price or part of $500.

faqs.q: Can I record documents by mail in Davidson County?
faqs.a: Military discharges and assumed business name filings can be mailed to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The assumed business name fee is $26.00, and a stamped return envelope is needed for return.
